outcome.technical:
drive-phase.run_verb now runs the verb in bytes mode: stdin is sent as stdin.encode('utf-8') (None stays None) with no text wrapper, so Windows can no longer turn its newlines into CRLF; captured stdout/stderr go through a new _verb_text(), which decodes UTF-8 with 'replace' and applies the same 
 /  -> 
 translation text mode applied (the body of CPython's Popen._translate_newlines, read with inspect on 3.14.7), so every caller keeps the str it parsed before. Every run_verb caller passes str stdin (json.dumps or the submit text) and reads str back. audit-lookup.write_brief and read_brief already open with encoding='utf-8', newline='' (lines 1437 and 1474), and write_exact already writes UTF-8 bytes to the buffer, so audit-lookup.py and test_audit_lookup.py were left unchanged. test_drive_phase.py: new _windows_text_run stand-in, which applies Windows' text-mode stdin translation to str input and passes bytes through; new case _stdin_bytes_case, run at the end of the dsm-block, which swaps the driver copy's subprocess for the stand-in, files a return through submit in-process, and asserts the filed file and the bytes file-return received are LF with no . On HEAD's driver it was red: the filed bytes began b'{
  "gates"...'. New _brief_difference(role, wrote, shown) returns None or (role, first differing offset, repr of 20 chars either side, written and shown). sn6 now reads the written brief as bytes and reports every mismatch through it. New _brief_difference_case runs at the head of sn5-block on a CRLF-vs-LF pair. In the shared tree it went red against a stub that returned only (role,), before the helper was written. On HEAD it is green, because what it tests lives in the test file itself. Runs: --stage dsm-block --stage sn5-block, 10/10 cases (8/10 before the fix). Full test_drive_phase --selftest, 297/297, exit 0. Plain sweep exit 0, 335/335 files ok. cp1252 sweep exit 1: the only failure is plugins/audit/tests/test__panel_discovery.py (UnicodeDecodeError: 'ascii' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 in position 107), a file outside this task. test_drive_phase.py and test_audit_lookup.py were ok in that pass. ruff exit 0. vermin exit 0.
outcome.descriptive: A return filed through submit now has the same LF bytes on every platform, and sn6 says which brief differs, where, and how.

testsAdded: a verb's stdin reaches it as the exact UTF-8 bytes it was given, with no newline translation, so a return filed through submit is byte-identical on every platform
a brief read back that differs from the written brief is reported with its role, the first differing offset and both sides around it
